test_title: PYST 06: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in Direct to Indirect Speech.

She said, "I had eaten breakfast."

options.text: She said that she ate breakfast.
She said that she would have eaten breakfast.
she said that she had eaten breakfast.
She said that she has eaten breakfast.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** She said that she had eaten breakfast.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"I had eaten breakfast" becomes "she had eaten breakfast"**
 
 
• Pronoun "I" is changed to "she" to match the subject of the reporting verb.
 
• Past perfect tense "had eaten" remains unchanged in indirect speech.
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• Indirect: "She said" introduces the statement.
 
• No change is required for the reporting verb in this case.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is converted to indirect speech by removing quotation marks.
 
• Conjunction "that" is used to connect the reporting verb and the reported speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said that she had eaten breakfast."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "She said that she ate breakfast." 

 
 
• Incorrect tense: "ate" (simple past) changes the meaning of the original sentence, which is in past perfect tense.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "She said that she would have eaten breakfast." 
 
 
• Incorrect modal verb: "would have" alters the original meaning, implying a conditional action.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "She said that she has eaten breakfast." 
 
 
• Incorrect tense: "has eaten" (present perfect) does not match the past perfect tense in the original sentence.
